Here is a transcription of the historical parish register entries visible in **image_2b29e2.png**.

The document is written in Latin, typical of 19th-century Catholic parish records, organized by month and day (*Die*). Each entry generally follows the formula: *Name of child, filius/filia (son/daughter) of [Father's Name] et [Mother's Name]. Sponsore/Sponsores (Sponsors/Godparents) [Names].* Most entries are signed off by the priest, *Joannes Quinlan C.C.* (Catholic Curate).

Due to the tight, cursive script, fading ink, and binding shadows, certain letters are partially obscured. Brackets `[ ]` indicate inferred text or standard abbreviations expanded for clarity.

> **Note on "In Ergastulo":** A few entries contain the parenthetical notation *(In Ergastulo)* next to the date. In church Latin context, this typically denotes a baptism performed in a local house of correction, prison, or institutional workhouse hospital.
